title: AUB Q1 Deep Dive: Loan Growth, Deposit Mix Shifts, and Integration Drive Strategic Focus
content:
Regional banking company Atlantic Union Bankshares (NYSE:AUB) missed Wall Street’s revenue expectations in Q1 CY2026, but sales rose 71.1% year on year to $371.7 million. Its non-GAAP profit of $0.89 per share was 2.2% above analysts’ consensus estimates.

Is now the time to buy AUB? Find out in our full research report (it’s free).

Atlantic Union Bankshares (AUB) Q1 CY2026 Highlights:

Revenue: $371.7 million vs analyst estimates of $381.8 million (71.1% year-on-year growth, 2.6% miss) Adjusted EPS: $0.89 vs analyst estimates of $0.87 (2.2% beat) Adjusted Operating Income: $168.2 million vs analyst estimates of $181.2 million (45.2% margin, 7.2% miss) Market Capitalization: $5.37 billion

StockStory’s Take

Atlantic Union Bankshares’ first quarter saw the market respond negatively, as revenue missed Wall Street expectations despite notable year-on-year growth. Management attributed the quarter’s results to continued loan growth, a successful integration of Sandy Spring Bank, and disciplined expense management. CEO John Asbury pointed to record fundings from the equipment finance group and strong production from the North Carolina commercial real estate team as bright spots, but also acknowledged elevated loan payoffs late in the quarter, particularly in commercial real estate, which offset some of the loan growth momentum.

Looking forward, management’s outlook centers on achieving loan growth within targeted ranges, maintaining expense discipline, and capitalizing on opportunities in attractive markets such as North Carolina. Executives highlighted robust loan pipelines and the expectation that higher interest rates will keep lending activity stable. CFO Alex Dodd emphasized the strategic focus on core deposit growth and indicated that the completion of merger integration would allow results to better reflect underlying operational performance. Asbury noted, “Our primary focus is on growing customer deposits and expanding our share of wallet.”

Key Insights from Management’s Remarks

Management cited loan growth, expense control, and the integration of Sandy Spring Bank as key influences on the quarter, while calling out late-quarter commercial real estate payoffs and deposit mix shifts as areas of focus.

Loan growth momentum: The quarter saw strong loan production, including record levels from Atlantic Union Equipment Finance and the North Carolina commercial real estate group. However, higher-than-typical payoffs in commercial real estate, driven by property sales, reduced net loan growth in the final weeks of the quarter. Deposit mix management: Management emphasized reducing high-cost brokered deposits and growing core customer deposits. Brokered deposits now represent only 2% of total deposits, and executives noted that the franchise’s core deposit base is a critical differentiator and central to funding strategy. Credit quality stability: Asset quality indicators continued to improve, with very low net charge-offs and declining nonperforming assets. The company also updated its credit loss reserve methodology, enhancing granularity and aligning with portfolio mix changes, which management believes should provide more precise monitoring of credit risk going forward. Expense discipline post-merger: Noninterest expenses decreased, mainly due to the end of merger-related costs and lower professional services and technology expenses. Management expects expense levels to remain well controlled, with some expected increases tied to North Carolina expansion later in the year. Integration and strategic refocus: The quarter marked the conclusion of Sandy Spring Bank integration, and with no new acquisitions planned in the near term, management is shifting focus to demonstrating earnings power and capital generation from the expanded footprint. Leadership views this as a pivotal transition for the company’s strategic plan.

Story Continues

Drivers of Future Performance

Management expects loan pipeline conversion, deposit growth, and operational efficiency to be the main themes shaping performance for the remainder of the year.

North Carolina expansion: The company is investing in new branch openings in the Raleigh and Wilmington areas, aiming to build on strong commercial loan momentum in the Carolinas. Management expects these markets to be key growth drivers due to favorable demographics and employment trends. Deposit cost pressures: Executives acknowledged heightened competition for deposits, especially in the Metro D.C. and North Carolina markets. The company is offering higher rates on CDs and money market accounts to attract new funds, which is expected to cause a modest increase in deposit costs throughout the year. Credit and margin management: The updated credit reserve model is designed to provide more granular risk management as the loan portfolio grows. While management projects net charge-off ratios to remain low, they cautioned that unforeseen one-off events could cause volatility. The outlook for net interest margin remains stable to slightly higher, supported by repricing of maturing fixed-rate loans at higher yields.

Catalysts in Upcoming Quarters

Looking ahead, analysts will monitor (1) loan growth conversion rates, especially in the Carolinas, (2) the pace and cost of new deposit inflows amid rising competition, and (3) the impact of North Carolina branch expansion on both loan and deposit growth. Developments in credit quality and margin management, as well as the company’s ability to control expenses post-integration, will also be important markers of execution.

Release Date: April 21, 2026

For the complete transcript of the earnings call, please refer to the full earnings call transcript.

Positive Points

Atlantic Union Bankshares Corp (NYSE:AUB) reported solid first-quarter financial results, reflecting disciplined execution and successful integration of Sandy Spring Bank. Quarterly loan growth was approximately 2.2% annualized, with total loans ending at $27.9 billion, showcasing strong loan production. The company experienced record-level fundings from Atlantic Union Equipment Finance and record-level production from the North Carolina-based commercial real estate team. Credit quality continues to show strength and improvement, with a first-quarter annualized net charge-off ratio of just two basis points. The deposit base demonstrated strong customer deposit growth, nearly offsetting the planned reduction in high-cost broker deposits, indicating a robust liquidity strategy.

Negative Points

The company experienced elevated payoffs late in the quarter, particularly within the commercial real estate portfolio, due to property sales. Net interest margin declined by 11 basis points to 3.85%, mainly due to lower accretion income compared to the previous quarter. Non-interest income declined by $2.2 million, primarily driven by lower loan-related interest rate swap fees. The geopolitical conflict in Iran and the resulting increase in petroleum prices pose potential risks to consumer and business confidence. The company lowered its full-year net interest income outlook due to increased deposit rate competition and lower purchase accounting accretion.

Story Continues

Q & A Highlights

Q: Can you provide insights on the core margin trend for the year and the direction of deposit costs with the Fed on pause? A: Rob Gorman, Senior Financial Advisor: We expect the core margin to grind higher as we don't anticipate Fed rate cuts this year. Deposit costs are likely to remain stable, with a slight potential increase. We have broker deposits maturing that currently pay high rates, which will be replaced at lower rates, positively impacting margins. Additionally, fixed-rate loan back book repricing will contribute to margin improvement.

Q: Is branch rationalization considered in the lowered expense guidance, and could it offset the lowered NII outlook? A: Rob Gorman, Senior Financial Advisor: Branch rationalization is not included in the current guidance. We maintain expense discipline and have lowered guidance due to better-than-expected first-quarter results. Seasonal expenses will decrease, and investments in North Carolina branches will start impacting expenses later this year.

Q: How do you expect core customer deposits and broker deposits to trend over 2026? A: Rob Gorman, Senior Financial Advisor: We anticipate 3% to 4% growth in core customer deposits. Broker deposits decreased significantly due to high costs and lower loan growth needs. We have maturing broker deposits this quarter and next, which will be replaced at lower rates if needed, depending on loan growth.

Q: Can you discuss the impact of the Basel III endgame proposal on Atlantic Union and your buyback plans? A: Rob Gorman, Senior Financial Advisor: The Basel III proposal could increase our CET1 regulatory capital ratio by 65 to 75 basis points. We plan to request board approval for share buybacks once we reach a 10.5% CET1 ratio, expected by Q2, and aim to be in the market soon after.

Q: What is the outlook for loan growth and its impact on NII guidance? A: Rob Gorman, Senior Financial Advisor: The NII guidance assumes lower loan growth than projected internally. If loan growth is flat, it could impact guidance, but we have levers like expense management and deposit cost adjustments to maintain margins. We expect loan growth to ramp up, supported by strong pipelines and production.

title: Atlantic Union Bankshares Corporation Q1 2026 Earnings Call Summary
content:
Atlantic Union Bankshares Corporation Q1 2026 Earnings Call Summary - Moby

Strategic Execution and Performance Drivers

Management successfully concluded the Sandy Spring Bank integration, marking the end of merger-related charges and noise starting next quarter. Loan growth of 2.2% annualized was impacted by elevated payoffs in the commercial real estate portfolio due to property sales, which management views as a sign of market liquidity and strength. Core customer deposits are described as the 'crown jewel' of the franchise, with growth in this area nearly offsetting the planned reduction of high-cost broker deposits. Net interest margin (NIM) expansion of 4 basis points, excluding accretion, was driven by lower deposit costs and the repricing of the fixed-rate loan back-book. Credit quality remains robust with a net charge-off ratio of only 2 basis points, though management maintains a conservative full-year projection of 10 to 15 basis points. The bank is transitioning from a period of strategic M&A to a phase focused on demonstrating earnings power and capital generation through organic growth in Virginia and the Carolinas.

2026 Outlook and Strategic Assumptions

Guidance assumes the Federal Reserve will not cut interest rates in 2026, leading to a 'higher for longer' environment that supports a gradual grind higher in core NIM. Loan balances are projected to reach $29 billion to $30 billion by year-end, supported by a construction and development pipeline that has reached record highs. The bank plans to invest in the North Carolina market by opening 10 new branches through 2028, with the first 3 expected by the end of 2026. Management expects to achieve a CET1 ratio above 10.5% by the end of Q2, which would trigger a request for share buyback authorization from the Board of Directors. Full-year tax equivalent NIM is projected between 3.90% and 4%, inclusive of an estimated $140 million to $145 million in loan accretion income.

Structural Changes and Risk Factors

Finalized Sandy Spring acquisition goodwill at $541 million following the conclusion of the one-year measurement period. Implemented a new 3-segment allowance for credit losses (ACL) model to provide more granular monitoring of Commercial Real Estate, C&I, and Consumer portfolios. Management is monitoring geopolitical tensions in Iran, noting that while direct credit risk is limited, potential petroleum price shocks could impact consumer and business confidence. A $3.5 million nonrecurring loan fair value adjustment was recorded this quarter, impacting reported accretion income.

Sustainability of core margin expansion and deposit cost trends

DATE

Full Conference Call Transcript

Bill Cimino: Thank you, Michelle, and good morning, everyone. I have Atlantic Union Bankshares Corporation’s President and CEO, John C. Asbury, and Executive Vice President and CFO, Alex Stodd, with me today. Since Alex is only eight days into his job, former CFO Robert Michael Gorman will cover the first quarter financial results in his transition capacity as a senior financial adviser to the company through his September 30 retirement. We also have other members of our executive management team with us for the question-and-answer period. Please note that today’s earnings release and the accompanying slide presentation we are going through on this webcast are available to download on our investor website investors.atlanticunionbank.com.

During today’s call, we will comment on our financial performance using both GAAP metrics and non-GAAP financial measures. Important information about these non-GAAP financial measures, including reconciliations to comparable GAAP measures, is included in the appendix to our slide presentation and in our earnings release for 2026. We will also make forward-looking statements, which are not statements of historical fact and are subject to risks and uncertainties. There can be no assurance that actual performance will not differ materially from any future expectations or results expressed or implied by these forward-looking statements. We undertake no obligation to publicly revise or update any forward-looking statement except as required by law.

Please refer to our earnings release and slide presentation issued today and our other SEC filings for further discussion of the company’s risk factors and other important information regarding our forward-looking statements, including factors that could cause actual results to differ from those expressed or implied in the forward-looking statements. All comments made during today’s call are subject to that Safe Harbor statement. At the end of the call, we will take questions from the research analyst community. I will now turn the call over to John.

John C. Asbury: Thank you, Bill. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. I am pleased to introduce Alex Stodd as our new Chief Financial Officer. Alex brings a wealth of experience having successfully helped guide a smaller institution through its transformation into a larger, more complex financial organization. His background aligns well with our executive leadership team, and I am confident he will add tremendous value as we continue to drive growth and innovation. Over the next few months, we look forward to having Alex meet many of you during our active investor relations calendar.

Story Continues

While Robert Michael Gorman will remain with us full-time until his retirement in September, I do want to extend my sincere gratitude to Rob for his invaluable contributions and dedication to ensuring a seamless CFO transition. Atlantic Union Bankshares Corporation reported solid first quarter financial results reflecting disciplined execution and a successful conclusion of the integration of Sandy Spring Bank. We believe the adjusted operating financial results for the quarter showcased the organization’s earnings capacity. We had a final set of merger-related charges impact this quarter’s results; underlying operating performance supports our continued confidence in achieving the financial outlook for adjusted operating return on assets, return on tangible common equity, and efficiency ratio that we have set for 2026.

We look forward to reporting results without the merger noise starting next quarter, which we believe should more clearly demonstrate the financial strength and operational efficiency that we are committed to delivering for our shareholders. Our commitment to creating shareholder value remains unwavering. We believe Atlantic Union Bankshares Corporation is well positioned to deliver sustainable growth, top-tier financial performance, and long-term value for our shareholders. We believe the strategic advantages gained from the Sandy Spring acquisition, combined with continued organic growth opportunities due to our robust presence in attractive markets, reinforce our status as the premier regional bank headquartered in the Lower Mid-Atlantic.

I will briefly cover the Q1 2026 highlights and share market insights before Rob presents the financial review. Here are the highlights from the first quarter. Quarterly loan growth was approximately 2.2% annualized during the typically slow first quarter, with total loans ending at $27.9 billion. For additional context, average quarterly loan growth over this year’s first quarter was roughly 5.9% annualized. Loan production remained strong and, when compared to the previous four quarters, was second only to the fourth quarter of last year. We were pleased to see record-level fundings from Atlantic Union Equipment Finance and record-level production from our North Carolina-based commercial real estate team.

However, we also experienced elevated payoffs late in the quarter, particularly within our commercial real estate portfolio due to a number of property sales. This activity highlights the strength of our CRE markets, robust investor demand, and the availability of ample liquidity. The first quarter saw a slight increase in line-of-credit utilization from the fourth quarter and was relatively flat year-over-year. At the end of the first quarter, our loan pipelines were noticeably higher than at the beginning, giving us confidence that we are pacing to meet our loan growth targets for 2026. A deeper look at the pipeline report reveals that our construction and development pipeline has achieved a record high.

For those familiar with my construction lending bathtub analogy, this means our pipeline is filling up at a faster rate than it is draining, which positions us well for continued growth in construction lending balances throughout the year. Forecasting loan growth remains challenging in this uncertain macroeconomic environment, particularly with the recent energy price shocks. We continue to expect 2026 year-end loan balances to range between $29 billion and $30 billion. Our deposit base demonstrated strong customer deposit growth this quarter, nearly offsetting the planned reduction in high-cost brokered deposits. Brokered deposits currently represent just 2% of total deposits and play a purposeful role in our liquidity strategy.

We believe this approach provides us flexibility to add brokered deposits in the future if needed. Depending on cost and market conditions, we anticipate any new additions, if any, would be at lower rates than those currently rolling off. Above all, our core customer deposit base remains the crown jewel of the franchise, and our primary focus is on growing customer deposits and expanding our share of wallet. Net interest margin, excluding the impact of accretion income, which can be volatile, improved by 4 basis points quarter-over-quarter, matching our expectations. Reported FTE net interest margin declined 11 basis points to 3.85%, mainly because accretion income was lower compared to the elevated level seen in Q4 2025.

Rob will provide more detail about the factors influencing NIM performance in his section. Credit quality continues to show strength and improvement. Our first quarter annualized net charge-off ratio was just 2 basis points. For the year, we are still projecting a range of 10 to 15 basis points, although we do not yet have full visibility into reaching that range. Key asset quality indicators remain robust and are improving. Nonperforming assets as a percentage of loans held for investment declined by 6 basis points to 0.36% from 0.42% in the prior quarter, bringing us closer to our historical operating levels. Criticized and classified assets also improved, decreasing to 4.5% of total loans from 4.7% last quarter.

Looking at the most current unemployment data, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported Virginia’s January unemployment rate remained stable at 3.7%. Maryland’s unemployment rate was 4.3%, and North Carolina’s was 3.8%, all of which are at or below January’s national average of 4.3%. We continue to expect unemployment levels in Virginia, Maryland, and North Carolina to stay manageable and comparable to or below the national average, consistent with Moody’s current state-level forecast. We remain confident in our markets and consider them among the most attractive in the country. I do want to acknowledge the ongoing conflict in Iran and its potential impact on our bank and the markets we serve.

We are closely monitoring the geopolitical developments and their effects on the broader economy. The most immediate consequence has been the sharp increase in petroleum prices. It is very important to understand how diversified Atlantic Union Bank is — we need to do a better job of explaining we are diversified over three very good states, and we have specialty lines like equipment finance that go beyond. We feel good about our opportunity.

Stephen Moss: Appreciate all the color. Thank you very much, guys.

John C. Asbury: Great. Thank you all so much. Take care. Thanks, everyone, for joining us. We look forward to talking with you next quarter.
